material_systems.name: Exterior Acrylic Field Primer for Fiber Cement

products: Benjamin Moore Ultra Spec EXT Primer
PPG Sun Proof Exterior Latex Primer
primer.notes: Standard acrylic exterior primer for field prime over factory primer on fiber cement. Factory prime is transit protection only — field prime is MANDATORY per James Hardie warranty. Must be top-coated within 180 days of installation.

material_systems.notes: Primary primer system for NC fiber cement. Factory-primed fiber cement has low porosity — higher coverage than bare wood. Field prime is required regardless of factory prime condition.

material_systems.name: Alkali-Resistant Primer for Bare Fiber Cement

products: Benjamin Moore Ultra Spec Masonry & Stucco Primer
primer.notes: Required for bare fiber cement (pH 13.0). Prevents saponification (alkaline burn) of latex binders. SW Loxon Masonry Primer is the reference product per field experience. Standard acrylic primer is NOT suitable for bare fiber cement. Apply within 90 days of exposure.

material_systems.notes: Lower coverage than standard acrylic primer — bare fiber cement is more porous at cut edges and damaged areas. Critical for preventing FM-002 (alkaline burn).

material_systems.name: Bonding Primer for Factory-Finished Fiber Cement

products: Benjamin Moore Insl-X Stix Bonding Primer
primer.notes: Required for ColorPlus/ExpertFinish factory-finished fiber cement. The oven-baked factory finish is a non-standard substrate for field paint adhesion — bonding primer provides mechanical grip on the cured factory topcoat. Light scuff sand entire surface before priming.

material_systems.notes: Factory-finished surfaces are smooth and non-porous — good coverage. Key is adhesion, not sealing. Per research RC-001 — common NC scenario where factory finish is compromised during construction.

material_systems.name: Standard Exterior Acrylic Finish for Fiber Cement

finish.notes: Hardie-approved products required for warranty compliance. QT2 allows single finish coat on properly primed surfaces. QT3 requires 2 coats standard.

material_systems.notes: Standard exterior production system. Flat is typical for siding field. Satin for accent or higher visibility areas. Fiber cement is non-porous after priming — consistent, predictable coverage.

material_systems.name: Premium Exterior Finish for Fiber Cement

finish.notes: James Hardie-approved premium products. Superior color retention, fade resistance. Light sand between coats on visible areas. Raking light inspection before second coat.

material_systems.notes: Premium exterior system for QT4 fiber cement work. Semi-gloss available at QT4 for high-visibility accent areas.

SS_EXT_PRIMED_FACTORY.notes: Factory-primed surface is sealed — consistent primer absorption. Smooth surface baseline.

assumptions: Coverage rates are for smooth surfaces. Apply surface_texture_modifier for textured profiles.
Spray application: multiply material quantity by 1.25-1.33 for 50-70% transfer efficiency.

SS_EXT_BARE_FIBERCEMENT.notes: Bare fiber cement at cut edges and damaged areas is more porous. Lower coverage than standard primer on factory-primed surface.

assumptions: Bare fiber cement exposure is typically localized (cut edges, damaged areas) — not full-field.
In full-field bare scenarios (entire siding removed factory prime), coverage drops further.

lap.notes: Smooth lap siding on primed surface. Consistent, predictable coverage. Long horizontal runs.

panel.notes: Large flat panels. Slightly better coverage than lap due to fewer edges and transitions.

shingle.notes: Many edges, overlapping profiles, complex geometry. Higher material consumption than lap or panel.

assumptions: Coverage is per NET siding area from PaintScope (PS_EXT_SURFACE_SF.SIDING_FIELD).
Two-coat system is standard at QT3/QT4. QT2 may use single coat.
Spray application: multiply material quantity by 1.25-1.33 for transfer efficiency loss.

consumables.name: Fiber cement end-cut edge sealer
consumables.notes: Seals field-cut edges to prevent capillary moisture absorption via cellulose fibers. Critical for preventing FM-001 (edge wicking). Apply to ALL field-cut edges.

consumables.name: Exterior flexible paintable caulk
consumables.notes: Polyurethane or siliconized acrylic for siding-to-trim joints. Do NOT caulk field butt joints on lap siding — creates moisture trap behind joint.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 150-180 grit
consumables.notes: For adhesion sanding on factory-primed and factory-finished surfaces. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 220 grit
consumables.notes: For intercoat sanding at QT4. Light scuff between finish coats. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Airless spray tip 517 (lap/panel siding)
consumables.notes: 515 or 517 fan pattern for lap and panel siding profiles. Cementitious substrate may cause slightly faster tip wear than wood.

consumables.name: Airless spray tip 413 (shingle profile)
consumables.notes: Smaller fan pattern for shingle profiles — complex geometry requires tighter spray pattern. Higher tip wear due to constant angle changes.

consumables.name: 60-mesh spray filter (black) for latex
consumables.notes: Standard 60-mesh (black) filter for latex exterior coatings through airless equipment. Change when flow rate drops.

consumables.name: Plastic sheeting / landscape tarps
consumables.notes: 4 mil minimum for landscape, hardscape, and HVAC unit protection. UV-resistant for multi-day exterior projects.

consumables.name: Painter's tape (exterior grade)
consumables.notes: UV-resistant exterior masking tape. 14-day removal rating minimum for multi-day exterior projects. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Canvas drop cloths
consumables.notes: Heavy canvas drop cloths for hardscape walkway and patio protection. Non-slip surface for crew traffic. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Tack cloth
consumables.notes: For dust removal after sanding before prime or finish coat. Reused consumable ID.

ext_landscape_perimeter.description: House perimeter where landscape is adjacent — measured in LF along foundation/siding line
ext_landscape_perimeter.notes: LF-based. Lay tarps along the perimeter of the house where landscape beds, shrubs, and plants are adjacent. Brush/roll: drop cloth at base. Spray: full tarp width over plantings.

ext_hardscape_walk.notes: Canvas drop cloths for non-slip crew traffic. Plastic sheeting for spray overspray.

ext_hardscape_patio.notes: Protection level driven by proximity and application method.

ext_light_fixture.description: Exterior light fixtures on or adjacent to siding
ext_light_fixture.notes: Bag or tape over fixture. Remove fixture cover plate if accessible.

ext_hvac_unit.description: HVAC condenser units adjacent to siding
ext_hvac_unit.notes: Full tarp cover during spray operations. Do not block intake/exhaust if unit is running.

compatibility_rules.description: Alkali-resistant primer required for bare fiber cement
compatibility_rules.notes: Standard acrylic primer on bare fiber cement (pH 13.0) causes saponification. Alkali-resistant primer is non-negotiable.

compatibility_rules.description: Bonding primer required for factory-finished surfaces
compatibility_rules.notes: Oven-baked factory finish requires bonding primer for adhesion. Acrylic primer lacks adhesion on cured factory coating. Alkali-resistant primer not needed — factory finish neutralizes pH.

compatibility_rules.description: No primer needed for field-primed surfaces
compatibility_rules.notes: Direct topcoat on field-primed surfaces. Skip prime module entirely.

compatibility_rules.description: Hardie-approved finish products for warranty compliance
compatibility_rules.notes: James Hardie warranty requires approved paint products. SW Duration, SW Emerald, BM Aura, and BM Regal Select are approved. Verify PDS compatibility for any substitution.

compatibility_rules.description: No power washing on fiber cement
compatibility_rules.notes: High-pressure power washing is PROHIBITED on fiber cement. Strips paint films, damages surface texture, forces water behind wall assembly. Low-pressure wash only (garden hose + soft brush).

risk_notes.risk: Unsealed field-cut edges absorb water via cellulose capillaries, causing edge swelling that ruptures paint film. Most common fiber cement failure mode.
risk_notes.mitigation: Seal ALL field-cut edges with end-cut sealer (CON_FCSD_END_SEALER) before or immediately after installation.

risk_notes.topic: Alkaline burn on bare fiber cement
risk_notes.risk: Standard latex primer on bare fiber cement (pH 13.0) causes saponification — paint softens, blisters, detaches.
risk_notes.mitigation: Use alkali-resistant primer (SYS_EXT_FC_PRIMER_ALKALI) on all bare fiber cement. Reference product: SW Loxon Masonry Primer.

risk_notes.risk: Factory primer degrades if exposed beyond 180 days. Becomes chalky, loses adhesion.
risk_notes.mitigation: Field-prime and paint within 180 days of installation. If exposure exceeds 180 days, assess adhesion with tape pull test. May require sanding and re-priming.

risk_notes.risk: Airless spray overspray drifts 10-15 ft. Can damage plantings, stain concrete, coat vehicles.
risk_notes.mitigation: Full landscape/hardscape protection for spray applications. Wind monitoring — stop spray if wind exceeds 10 mph.

risk_notes.risk: Field painting over factory-finished (ColorPlus) fiber cement voids the factory finish warranty.
risk_notes.mitigation: Document customer authorization before field-painting factory-finished products. The factory finish warranty is replaced by the field paint system warranty.

material_quantity_notes.spray_transfer_efficiency: Airless spray on fiber cement siding: 50-70% transfer efficiency. Multiply theoretical coverage by 1.25-1.50 to account for overspray, misting, and pattern overlap.
material_quantity_notes.surface_texture_factor: Cedarmill texture: multiply material by 1.20x. Roughsawn texture: multiply by 1.30x. Applied on top of profile coverage rate.
material_quantity_notes.two_coat_standard: Standard coat system: 1 field prime + 2 finish coats at QT3/QT4. QT2 may use single finish coat. SS_EXT_PRIMED_FIELD skips prime coat.
material_quantity_notes.shingle_profile_premium: Shingle profile consumes 25-35% more material than lap siding due to complex geometry and edge coverage.

assumptions.note: Fiber cement is less porous than bare wood — better primer coverage than wood siding.

assumptions.value: Single finish coat acceptable at QT2 on primed surfaces
assumptions.note: QT2 economy tier allows single coat — reduced labor and material.

assumptions.value: Shingle profile rates extrapolated from wood shingle rates
assumptions.source: Research uncertainty — no direct fiber cement shingle calibration
assumptions.note: Fiber cement shingles may differ slightly from wood shingles. Flag for field calibration.
